identity.name: Kubernetes-Goat Container Escape Chain — Cortex Cloud CDR (T1611 / T1610)
identity.summary: Drive the Kubernetes-Goat vulnerable cluster's escape paths (DIND/docker.sock abuse, nsenter into the host PID namespace, host-path mount access, and high-capability exploitation) against the cdr EKS lab. The BIOC/XQL detect the escape-to-host primitives and resulting host-process activity Cortex Cloud CDR + XSIAM must surface.
identity.description: This scenario ports the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab panw-goat fixture (Madhu Akula's Kubernetes-Goat) into a Cortex Cloud CDR detection card, complementing SIM-CDR-003's single-vector escape with a full escape-chain. Kubernetes-Goat ships intentionally vulnerable workloads — DIND (docker-in-docker) with an exposed docker.sock, an SSRF proxy, a system-monitor pod that allows container escape, and a poor-registry — and the lab's access script port-forwards each so an operator can exercise them. CortexSim reproduces the four canonical escape primitives the goat cluster enables, drawn from the lab's container-escape.sh: (1) docker.sock abuse — a container with the host Docker socket mounted runs `docker run -v /:/host` to chroot the host root; (2) nsenter into the host PID/mount/net namespaces from a privileged container; (3) direct access to a mounted host filesystem path (/host/etc, /host/root); and (4) exploitation of a container holding full (0xffffffffffffffff) effective capabilities. None of these require detonating a real exploit binary — each is a process/file telemetry shape produced by standard tooling (docker, nsenter, cat) that the scenario runs against benign targets inside the lab. A BIOC fires on the DIND/nsenter/host-namespace escape primitive (T1611 Escape to Host); a second BIOC fires on a container reading or writing a mounted host-path directory; and an XQL surfaces the host-process activity that follows a successful escape (a container-origin process now executing in the host namespace). A correlation rule fuses the escape primitive and the resulting host-process activity into one container-escape-chain incident, and the reusable container-workload projection attributes each event to its pod, image, and container_id. This proves Cortex covers the breadth of escape paths a real intruder pivots through, not just a single vector.

actors.name: Opportunistic container intruders abusing misconfigured/privileged workloads

campaigns: Container escape to host via misconfigured Kubernetes workloads

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-011 — Kubernetes-Goat escape-chain primitives for Cortex Cloud CDR validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR connected to the EKS cluster with the Linux agent daemonset deployed so per-container process + file telemetry reaches xdr_data.
prerequisites.check_command: kubectl -n kube-system get daemonset | grep -i cortex

prerequisites.description: cdr IaC module applied and a privileged / docker.sock-mounted / host-path workload available to exec into (the goat-equivalent vulnerable pods).

payload.code:
# Escape-chain primitives drawn from panw-goat/container-escape.sh. Each is a
# detectable process/file shape run against benign targets in the lab cluster —
# no real exploit binary is detonated and host data is only read, not modified.
set -euo pipefail
# (1) docker.sock abuse
if [ -S /var/run/docker.sock ]; then echo "[*] docker.sock present — escape via docker run -v /:/host stubbed [truncated]"; fi
# (2) nsenter into host namespaces from a privileged container
grep -q 'docker\|kubepods' /proc/1/cgroup 2>/dev/null && echo "[*] containerized PID 1 — nsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i sh stubbed [truncated]" || true
# (3) mounted host-path access
mount | grep -E '/host' && ls -la /host/etc /host/root 2>/dev/null || echo "[*] no /host mount in this pod"
# (4) high-capability exploitation
grep CapEff /proc/1/status | grep -q 'ffffffffffffffff' && echo "[*] full effective capabilities detected" || true

input_variables.name: TARGET_NS
input_variables.description: Namespace of the vulnerable/privileged goat workload to exec into.

expected_artifacts.description: nsenter invoked against PID 1 namespaces, or docker run mounting the host root, from inside a container.
Read or write of a mounted host-path directory (/host/etc, /host/root, /host/proc).

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-011 cleanup complete — no host artifacts modified; EKS cluster owned by terraform destroy.'

biocs.name: CDR-011 Container Escape via DIND nsenter or Host Namespace
biocs.description: A containerized process invokes nsenter against PID 1 namespaces or runs the Docker client with the host root bind-mounted (docker run -v /:/host), the canonical DIND/privileged-container escape primitives Kubernetes-Goat exposes (T1611 Escape to Host).
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter action_process_image_name in ("nsenter", "docker", "runc")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "-t 1" or action_process_image_command_line contains "/:/host" or action_process_image_command_line contains "--privileged"
| comp count() as escape_attempts by agent_hostname, action_process_image_name
| filter escape_attempts >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, action_process_image_name, escape_attempts

biocs.name: CDR-011 Host Path Mount Access from Container
biocs.description: A process inside a container reads or writes a mounted host-path directory (/host/etc, /host/root, /host/proc), the host-filesystem-breakout primitive used after a privileged or hostPath-mounted goat pod is reached (T1611 Escape to Host).
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter action_file_path contains "/host/etc" or action_file_path contains "/host/root" or action_file_path contains "/host/proc"
| comp count() as host_path_touches by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter host_path_touches >= 1
| sort desc host_path_touches
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, host_path_touches

xql_queries.name: CDR-011 Container Workload Projection
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| fields actor_container_info as container_info
| filter container_info != null
| alter pod_namespace = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_namespace")
| alter pod_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_name")
| alter image_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_name")
| alter image_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_id")
| alter container_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.id")
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.privileged")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("nsenter", "docker", "runc", "sh", "bash")

xql_queries.name: CDR-011 Container Escape to Host Process Activity
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("nsenter", "docker", "runc")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "chroot", "id", "cat")
| comp count() as host_proc_events by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter host_proc_events >= 1
| sort desc host_proc_events
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, host_proc_events

correlation_rules.name: Kubernetes-Goat Escape Chain — Escape Primitive Then Host Process Activity
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(CDR-011 Container Escape via DIND nsenter or Host Namespace) AND XQL(CDR-011 Container Escape to Host Process Activity) — fuses the escape primitive with the resulting host-namespace process activity into one container-escape-chain incident.

analytics_modules: Cortex Cloud CDR — container escape, host-namespace and docker.sock abuse detection
Cortex XSIAM Analytics — anomalous host-namespace process spawned from a container origin

products.evidence_query: dataset = xdr_data | filter actor_container_info != null | filter action_process_image_name in ("nsenter", "docker") or action_file_path contains "/host/"
Correlation CR-CDR-0011 fuses the escape-primitive BIOC and the host-process-activity XQL into one container-escape-chain incident.

threat_scenarios.name: Kubernetes Container Escape Chain Detection
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex Cloud CDR + XSIAM detect the breadth of container-escape primitives a Kubernetes-Goat-style cluster exposes — DIND/docker.sock abuse, nsenter into host namespaces, host-path access — and the resulting host-process activity.

threat_steps.objective: The escape primitives (nsenter / docker.sock / host-path) are detected.
preconditions: cdr EKS fixture applied with the Cortex Linux agent daemonset deployed.
A privileged / docker.sock-mounted / host-path goat workload available.
steps: Exec into the vulnerable workload and run the escape-chain primitives.
success_criteria: BIOC `CDR-011 Container Escape via DIND nsenter or Host Namespace` fires.
BIOC `CDR-011 Host Path Mount Access from Container` fires.

threat_steps.objective: The host-namespace process activity after escape is detected and stitched.
preconditions: Cortex agent ingestion active so host-namespace process events reach xdr_data.
steps: Run a shell in the entered host namespace.
Observe the host-process-activity XQL and CR-CDR-0011 escalate.
success_criteria: XQL `CDR-011 Container Escape to Host Process Activity` returns >= 1 host.
Correlation CR-CDR-0011 raises one container-escape-chain incident.

preventive_controls: Forbid privileged pods, hostPath volumes, hostPID/hostNetwork, and docker.sock mounts via admission control (OPA/Gatekeeper or Kyverno).
Drop ALL capabilities and apply a restrictive seccomp profile that blocks nsenter / mount / chroot inside workload containers.
Use a container runtime sandbox (gVisor/Kata) for untrusted workloads to harden the escape boundary.
detection_engineering: Alert on nsenter against PID 1 namespaces or docker run with the host root bind-mounted from inside a container.
Detect a container process reading or writing a mounted host-path directory.
Stitch an escape primitive to the resulting host-namespace process activity into one incident.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Initial CDR Kubernetes-Goat escape-chain card for SIM-CDR-011, porting the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab panw-goat fixture. Reproduced the four escape primitives (docker.sock, nsenter, host-path, high-cap) as detectable process/file shapes against benign lab targets. Authored two escape BIOCs, a host-process-activity XQL, the reusable container-workload projection hunt query, and correlation CR-CDR-0011. Promoted to active.
